newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Jet trades higher, diesel lower.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Jet trades higher, diesel lower.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel continued to trade higher on Wednesday, while gas oil traded slightly lower, traders said.

Jet fuel prices have been rising since April 24 when it traded at $24.25. On Wednesday another 100,000 barrels were sold by a Europen major to a Singapore trader at $25.50 per barrel for May 26-30 lifting free-on-board (fob) basis.
The buyer said jet fuel prices are rising to catch up with gas oil values.
The European major on Tuesday bought from a US trader at $25.24 for May 14-18 lifting fob.
The firmer physical jet fuel prices was also reflected in the swaps market where May regrade was bid at minus 30 cents against buyers at minus 65 cents on Tuesday.
Three cargoes of gas oil totalling 450,000 barrels exchanged hands on Wednesday.

A Singapore trader bought from a Swiss trader at $26.30 per barrel for May 26-30 lifting fob. Its sister company bought two cargoes--one from a US major at $26.30 for May 15-19 lifting and the second from a European major at $26.00 per barrel for May 26-30 lifting.
Traders noted that the backwardation on physical gas oil for May has almost flattened as interest started shifting to June.
They said one of the Singapore traders were actively selling both May and June swaps.
The backwardation on the swaps market is also narrowing, reflecting the weaker front month physical values.
Traders expected more active buying on Friday after the market takes a break on Thursday.
Traders said while the Singapore trader was said to be placing most of its massive gas oil purchases to China, it was also facing stiff competition for the lucrative market from South Korea.
They said that ships from major Korean sellers were seen not only headed to northern but also southern China which is the favourite haunt of most Singapore cargoes.

Sri Lanka was expected to award its gas oil and gasoline tender for May 21-22 delivery to Swiss trader Glencore. The 1.0-percent sulphur gas oil was offered at 38 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes and the 95-octane leaded gasoline was offered at a $1.85-premium, cost-and-freight Colombo.
